title: Design a Threaded Comment Ranking Platform
prompt:
Design ranking for threaded discussions. A comment belongs to one parent (a post or another comment), and ranking occurs only among that parent's direct children. Votes, replies, moderation actions, edits, and time affect the ranking policy. Readers need stable cursor pagination even while new votes arrive, and some parents can become extremely hot.

Cover:

- Idempotent event ingestion and the authoritative state for comments, votes, and moderation.
- A versioned scoring pipeline, per-parent sibling-list materialization, microbatching, and hysteresis for small score changes.
- Ranking generations and cursors that do not silently mix incompatible orderings.
- Cache invalidation, hot-parent isolation, replay, failure behavior, and ranking-quality/freshness metrics.

State what is exact, what is asynchronous, and what a reader should do when a ranking generation changes mid-pagination.

response.placeholder: Start with the direct-sibling ranking boundary. Then define idempotent event state, a versioned score projection per parent, generation-aware cursors, and a plan that keeps one hot parent from delaying every other thread.
response.reference_answer:
## 1. Assumptions and ranking contract

The rankable unit is one direct-sibling list: all comments with the same `parent_id`. A comment tree is not globally sorted. The API returns a materialized order for one parent, a `ranking_model_version`, a `generation`, and a cursor pinned to that generation. Scores may update asynchronously, so a fresh vote need not move a comment in the first read after acceptance. A reader who presents a cursor from an expired generation either continues against its retained snapshot for a bounded time or receives an explicit restart token; the API must not combine page one from one ordering with page two from another.

I would define one visible score formula version at a time, including vote treatment, age decay, moderator overrides, and anti-abuse penalties. The product must decide whether a removed comment stays as a tombstoned placeholder for cursor stability or disappears immediately; I assume a visibility change is a high-priority event that creates a new generation.

## 2. Authoritative events and projections

Comment creation, edits, moderation transitions, and votes enter a durable event log with immutable event IDs. A vote is also represented by an authoritative per `(actor_id, comment_id)` vote register, so retries and changing an upvote to a downvote create one current contribution rather than unbounded accumulated points. Event consumers use unique IDs and per-entity sequence checks, making replay safe. Raw comment metadata and moderation state are authoritative records; ranking is a rebuildable projection.

A parent-owner partition consumes the relevant events, maintains counters and features for that parent's direct children, and computes a score tagged with model version and feature timestamp. It writes a sibling-list projection ordered by `(score, deterministic_tie_breaker, comment_id)`. The list stores the source event watermark and generation so a query can name exactly what it read. A reply increments a separate reply feature for its immediate parent without forcing an unrelated grandparent list to be rescored.

## 3. Hot path, microbatches, and hysteresis

Votes may arrive much faster than readers need rank movement. The owner coalesces low-priority score events for a short microbatch window, then recomputes only affected siblings and publishes one new generation. Hysteresis prevents visual churn: a comment must exceed a neighboring score by a configurable margin, or remain beyond the boundary for a minimum interval, before it swaps positions. This rule is part of the versioned policy and is bypassed for removals or high-priority moderator actions.

The read service checks the cached sibling-list generation before returning a page. A cursor encodes parent ID, sort policy/model version, generation, and the last ordering tuple; it is authenticated or signed to prevent substitution. Cache updates are versioned publishes, not in-place mutations. The service can keep a small number of older generations or a compact page-boundary index so in-progress pagination has a defined bounded lifetime.

## 4. Hot-parent isolation, failures, and observability

Partition by `parent_id` so one viral discussion has a dedicated queue, rate budget, and owner shard rather than causing head-of-line blocking for unrelated threads. An exceptionally hot parent can be moved with a fenced ownership epoch, replaying from a watermark into a new owner before it serves writes. Vote ingestion can remain broadly partitioned, but its ranked projection events must converge at the parent owner. If that owner falls behind, serve its last published generation with an `as_of` watermark and prioritize moderation/visibility events over ordinary vote churn.

Monitor event duplicate rate, consumer lag by parent, microbatch size and delay, generation publication rate, cache age and hit rate, cursor restart rate, rank churn, moderation-to-removal latency, hot-parent queue depth, feature freshness, scoring failures by model version, and offline ranking-quality metrics such as engagement calibration, abuse catches, and diversity. Shadow-score a new model against replayed traffic before making its version visible.

## 5. Trade-offs

Per-parent materialization gives fast reads and a precise sibling-order contract, but stores more derived state than ranking on every request. Microbatching and hysteresis reduce write amplification and reader churn at the price of delayed small changes; the API must expose the freshness watermark instead of pretending every vote reordered the list immediately.

Retaining old generations improves pagination stability but consumes cache and projection storage. Forcing a restart is cheaper but more disruptive. Parent ownership preserves local order and isolates hotspots, while a single global ranking worker would simplify deployment but allow one viral thread to harm the whole product.

## Progressive Hints

1. Rank only comments that share the same direct parent.
2. Store current vote intent per actor and comment; do not add every retry as another vote.
3. Put model version and generation in both the stored order and the cursor.
4. A small score change does not always need an immediate visible reorder.
5. Route all ranking updates for a hot parent to an isolated authority, but keep unrelated parents independent.
